steps.title: Recruit and Screen Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit volunteers via advertisements and social media; calculate target sample size with G*Power; include only participants with normal or corrected‑to‑normal vision; exclude anyone with astigmatism >100°, strabismus, color blindness/weakness, serious ophthalmic disease, or medication affecting pupil response; require myopic participants to wear standard transparent glasses without any color‑filtering lenses (no blue‑light blocking, photochromic, sunglasses, etc.); perform comprehensive pre‑experiment visual screening.

steps.title: Give Pre‑Experiment Instructions
steps.instruction: Tell participants to obtain adequate rest, avoid caffeine and alcohol for 24 h before the experiment, and not wear eyelashes or makeup on the test day.

steps.title: Prepare Room and Equipment
steps.instruction: Set up a dimly lit experiment room containing a stimulus‑presentation computer, an eye‑data acquisition computer, and the SMI eye‑tracking system; place a stable chair and a chin rest with cheek and head rests; position the monitor 60 cm in front of and at the level of the eye tracker; the monitor should be 51 cm wide (48.92° visual angle) and 28.4 cm high (27.09° visual angle) and fully visible to the participant.

steps.title: Obtain Consent and Brief Participant
steps.instruction: On arrival, explain the purpose, procedure, risks, voluntary nature, confidentiality, and compensation; obtain written informed consent.

steps.title: Seat Participant and Adjust Hardware
steps.instruction: Have the participant sit on the stable chair, place the chin on the chin rest, and adjust the chair or chin‑rest height for comfort; support the head with the cheek and head rests; for infants, children, or participants with difficulty controlling head movements, consider using eye‑recording equipment with stickers or markers (e.g., Eyelink).

steps.title: Present Instructions and Verify Understanding
steps.instruction: Display the full on‑screen instruction block (welcome message, fixation cross, no‑blink request, break procedure, space‑bar to begin, total duration ~30 min, etc.); confirm the participant fully understands and has no questions.

steps.title: Run Practice Trials
steps.instruction: Guide the participant through a practice session of about five trials to familiarize them with the task; extend the practice if needed; for participants with reading difficulties, give oral instructions supplemented with visual aids.

steps.title: Configure Eye‑Tracker Settings
steps.instruction: Set the eye‑tracker sampling rate to 500 Hz (higher rates are available); record the left eye (or right/both if desired); note that binocular recording is recommended for microsaccade analysis.

steps.title: Generate Stimuli
steps.instruction: Use the Troje biological‑motion (BM) stimulus set; select a neutral walker (score 0), a happy walker (+6 SD on the linear emotion axis), and a sad walker (‑6 SD); rotate each upright walker 45° leftward or rightward to create intact BM; create inverted BM by vertically mirror‑flipping the upright BM; produce non‑biological motion by removing acceleration so each dot moves at a constant speed equal to its average speed; produce local BM by randomly relocating the 15 point‑light dots (head, pelvis, thorax, shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, ankles) within the original walker’s occupied region while preserving local motion; ensure all stimuli are centered on the screen.

steps.title: Calibrate Eye Tracker
steps.instruction: Perform a nine‑point calibration before the formal experiment; re‑calibrate after any accidental head movement or if validation indicates misalignment.

steps.title: Run Experimental Trials
steps.instruction: Execute the custom MATLAB script to present trials; each trial consists of: (1) a central fixation cross (0.2° × 0.2°) displayed for 800–1,200 ms to obtain a baseline pupil size; (2) an upright happy, sad, or neutral point‑light walker (45° left or right) shown centrally for 4,000 ms while the participant fixates and refrains from blinking; (3) after stimulus offset, the participant presses the space bar to continue; (4) a blank screen for 3,000 ms to allow pupil size to return to baseline.

steps.title: Structure Blocks and Breaks
steps.instruction: Organize the experiment into four blocks of 30 trials each; give a short break after each block; before each block, run an eye‑tracker validation; monitor head movement and, if movement occurs, repeat calibration; continuously watch real‑time eye data to ensure (i) fixation at the center, (ii) minimal blinking, and (iii) accurate pupil position and size capture.

steps.title: Post‑Block Check‑In
steps.instruction: After each block, ask the participant about their current state and ensure they take a full break (they may close their eyes) before proceeding.

steps.title: Administer Autism‑Spectrum Questionnaire
steps.instruction: At the end of all blocks, have the participant complete the 50‑item Autism‑Spectrum Quotient (AQ) questionnaire.

steps.title: Clean Equipment
steps.instruction: After the experiment, clean the eye‑tracking equipment using tissue paper, alcohol pads, or other appropriate cleaning items.
